papers.title: Five-year follow-up of a prospective randomised trial comparing ceramic-on-metal and metal-on-metal bearing surfaces in total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: AIMS: The primary aim of this independent prospective randomised trial was to compare serum metal ion levels for ceramic-on-metal (CoM) and metal-on-metal (MoM) bearing surfaces in total hip arthroplasty (THA). Our one-year results demonstrated elevation in metal ion levels above baseline with no significant difference between the CoM and MoM groups. This paper reviews the five-year data. PATIENTS AND METHODS: The implants used in each patient differed only in respect to the type of femoral head (ceramic or metal). At five-year follow-up of the 83 enrolled patients, data from 67 (36 CoM, 31 MoM) was available for comparison. RESULTS: The mean serum cobalt (Co) and chromium (Cr) ion levels remained above baseline in both groups (CoM: Co 1.16 μg/l (0.41 to 14.67), Cr 1.05 μg/l (0.16 to 12.58); MoM: Co 2.93 μg/l (0.35 to 30.29), Cr 1.85 μg/l (0.36 to 17.00)) but the increase was significantly less in the CoM cohort (Co difference p = 0.001, Cr difference p = 0.002). These medium-term results, coupled with lower revision rates from national joint registries, suggest that the performance of CoM THA may be superior to that of MoM. CONCLUSION: 2017;99-B:1298-1303.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文报告髋关节置换术后金属离子水平的临床随访结果，未涉及生物力学建模或有限元分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical trial comparing bearing surfaces with metal ion levels and revision rates; it contains no biomechanical modeling, contact mechanics, stress/strain analysis, or finite element simulation relevant to femoral stem design or validation.

summary_en.motivation: To compare long-term serum metal ion levels between ceramic-on-metal and metal-on-metal bearing surfaces in total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A prospective randomized trial with 83 patients, measuring serum cobalt and chromium at five-year follow-up.
summary_en.result: Ceramic-on-metal bearings showed significantly lower metal ion levels than metal-on-metal bearings at five years.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up at five years with 67 patients providing data.
